# Recipe — Emitter meets a Mirror Wall **A notebook `canvas` cell that runs a `buildExperiment(exp)` RECIPE.** Unlike the setup-factory galleries (`fn(frqtl, universe, options)`), this canvas declares `shape="recipe"`: the module installs a `buildExperiment(exp)` recipe (the same `exp.createCanvas()/addObject()` sketch form STUDIO saves and the Walk-through rungs run), and the shim builds a sizeless `RecipeContext` and calls `exp.build(buildExperiment)` for it. A spherical source of oppositely-charged quanta on the left sprays a disk of walks; a reflective **Wall** on the right bounces every arrival back on its axis of incidence. No wave equation — the mirror is a single-occupancy collision behavior. The recipe — a `buildExperiment(exp)` module. It creates the WORLD first — canvas and universe in one call, `exp.createCanvas(480, 480, …)`, the only place its size is written — then adds a `SphereEmitter` and a bounce/reflect `Wall`, exactly as a saved STUDIO project or a Walk-through rung would (parts never init the world). The sketch form — an ES module whose default export is `buildExperiment(exp)`, importing its parts from `@descix/frqtl-web/parts` — is the canonical recipe form. STUDIO writes a hand (a drag, an Inspector edit) back into a sketch's `export const parts` block with the parts writer, `exp.toSketch()`; this recipe adds its parts in code, so it is the sketch form without a parts block: /* buildExperiment(exp) — a mini emitter + mirror-wall RECIPE. * * The RecipeContext (`exp`) form, in the canonical two-step order every Walk-through * rung and every saved STUDIO project uses — WORLD FIRST, THEN PARTS: * * exp.createCanvas(W, H, SphereEmitter.worldCfg(SRC)); // 1. the world (and its canvas) * exp.addObject('SphereEmitter', SRC); // 2. the part * * `universe.init()` is a universe-GLOBAL reset (it clears every frame and fixes the * base dimension, wavelengthScale and active axes), so it belongs to the SKETCH and * runs ONCE, before any part is constructed. A PART never inits the world: both * ObjectFactory's SphereEmitter builder and the SphereEmitter part say so in as many * words, and the first engine registration a part makes throws * `EGPTUniverse.init() must be called before any simulation methods` on a world that * has not been init'd. * * ONE bag (`SRC`) feeds BOTH steps, so the world and the emitter can never disagree: * `SphereEmitter.worldCfg(bag)` is the ONE authority for the λ_eff chain * (fundamentalWaveLength → wavelengthScale → λ_eff = (capacity/mass) × * wavelengthScale) and for the 2D/3D axis selection — cite it, never a copied * constant. * * SU1: zero new physics — the SphereEmitter + Wall are already-goldened behaviors * (canonical-bench S* + LO1 Bounce/Reflect); the recipe only composes them. */ import { SphereEmitter } from '@descix/frqtl-web/parts'; export default function buildExperiment(exp) { var W = 480, H = 480; // THE WORLD this recipe states (its co-init call below) var cy = Math.round(H / 2); // A spherical source of oppositely-charged dim-2 leaves (the interference braiding // comes from the random ± charge). In 2D the ball-rejected sampler collapses to an // even disk of launch directions. This SAME bag is the world step's input. var SRC = { preset: 'spherical', is2D: true, center: [Math.round(W * 0.15), cy], chargeMode: 'random', fundamentalDimension: 2, wavelength: 32, burstSize: 24, emitEveryTicks: 1 }; // 1. THE WORLD the emitter implies, and its canvas, in one call. exp.createCanvas(W, H, SphereEmitter.worldCfg(SRC)); // 2. THE PARTS. exp.addObject('SphereEmitter', SRC); // A reflective wall — Bounce/Reflect inverts each arrival on its axis of incidence // (a real mirror, canonical-bench LO1). Drag/rotate it in STUDIO to steer. exp.addObject('Wall', { rect: [Math.round(W * 0.6), Math.round(H * 0.2), 20, Math.round(H * 0.6)], collisionBehavior: 'bounce', bounceDirection: 'reflect', name: 'mirror', color: [170, 190, 230] }); } Declare a `shape="recipe"` canvas that runs it. `setup=""` + `seed` — no `stage`: the recipe states its own world; the shim synthesizes a `RecipeContext` builder and runs it in the realm. Click **Run** (or **Run All**): ## What you are seeing The source on the left sprays a disk of charged quanta; those that reach the wall on the right reflect off it. The bright/dark structure in the beam is the emergent interference of the oppositely-charged walks — no wave function anywhere. **Edit the recipe:** open the `./setups/recipe-emitter-wall.js` tab, change the `wavelength`, `burstSize`, or the wall's `collisionBehavior` (`bounce` → `absorb` / `detect`), then re-Run. Because this is the `buildExperiment(exp)` recipe form, the same source round-trips through STUDIO Save and the Walk-through rungs.
